headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: OpenHands can write/egress broadly while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified docs-only agent with no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default-dangerous. However, OpenHands can use MCP and files in its runtime, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent/MCP-oriented repo; if outputs are manually bridged or mounted, injected content could be reinterpreted. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through a shared file, MCP server, or copy-paste bridge
IF OpenHands is configured to treat ai-engineering-hub output as instructions
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP server between the agents
Use a read-only handoff file with explicit delimiters
Add a human review step before OpenHands executes external text
Rename instruction-like sections in handoff artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands reads and writes files in its runtime and can egress broadly, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent repo with no stated isolation or data-handling limits. If both touch the same mounted workspace, file contents can flow from one to the other and then out via OpenHands. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible but not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same mounted volume or workspace
IF OpenHands is allowed to transmit file contents to its configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared mount before running either agent
Set OpenHands to offline or no-egress mode
Mount shared files read-only for one side
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; ai-engineering-hub is an agent/MCP repo with no declared locking or coordination. If both operate on the same repo or mounted directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Uncertainty remains about ai-engineering-hub's runtime, so severity is escalated.
conditions: IF both agents can write to the same directory or git checkout
IF neither side uses an external lock or serialized handoff
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Avoid shared git branches during concurrent runs
Use file locks for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files and browser/MCP outputs, so if it consumes ai-engineering-hub-generated text as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into edits or external actions. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, but the pathway exists because one agent can produce content and the other can execute it. OpenHands' action-taking authority makes verification important.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses ai-engineering-hub output as a plan, prompt, or code patch without verification
IF the output is forwarded into browser, shell, or MCP actions
mitigations: Require a human approval gate before execution
Compare outputs against a second source before acting
Restrict OpenHands to dry-run mode for the first pass
Mark generated text as untrusted in the handoff
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. OpenHands handles files in its runtime and model-provider API keys, while ai-engineering-hub is docs-only with no data-class claims. Because the pair lacks evidence of PHI, EU PII, or retention conflicts, compliance risk is limited to generic policy drift rather than a concrete breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into OpenHands' runtime files
IF the configured model provider or MCP server has retention terms that conflict with local policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared runtime
Review provider retention settings before use
Document a data-handling policy for both agents
Use separate accounts for each agent
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
